Development of Hybrid Model for the Air Pollution Dispersion Analysis and Community Exposure Assessment in an Opencast Coal Mine

Abstract:

This study provides an integrated assessment of dispersion of PM10, source contributions, and associated health risks around a highly mechanized opencast coal mine in India using field monitoring, chemical characterization, and coupled dispersion modelling. PM10 was monitored from January&ndashDecember 2024, and seasonal dispersion of mine and haul-road emissions was simulated using a coupled WRF&ndashAERMOD framework. The modelling and spatial interpolation revealed a persistent central plume core with PM10 peaks of 200-250 &microg m-3 in core zone declining to 40-50 &microg m-3 at the periphery, and extended transport corridors exceeding 80-100 &microg m-3 near operational pathways. Chemical analysis of PM10 filter papers using ICP-OES showed high crustal elements Al (92 ppm), Fe (72 ppm), Ca (126 ppm), Na (101 ppm), Zn (93 ppm) along with toxic metals such as Pb, Ni, Cd, Mn, Cr, and Be, several surpassing NAAQS or occupational limits.
